tools.description:
If you have not read tally://reference/logic and tally://reference/calculations yet, read them first (as MCP resources or with read_reference). Create, update or delete logic rules. Create/update use DSL syntax: WHEN THEN . To delete an existing rule, send `{operation: 'delete', blockUuid: }` — no dsl needed. Copy the uuid from the ledger's Logic rules table. This is the only way to remove a rule; never target a rule's condition or action uuids with other tools. CALCULATE and JUMP actions run only on the rule's own page, when the respondent visits it. SHOW, HIDE and REQUIRE apply on every page, so never copy those rules for placement. For a CALCULATE that every branch needs, insert one copy per branch, each with its branch's `page`. Without `page`, a rule that reads a calculated field lands after its last writer on any page, which can be another branch. All UUIDs come from the ledger. Use the correct column: - **Condition LHS** → questionUuid column - **Condition RHS for choice fields (Dropdown, MultipleChoice, Checkboxes)** → the option row's blockUuid (NOT the option text) - **Condition LHS for Matrix** → row blockUuid (MATRIX_ROW) - **Condition RHS for Matrix** → matrix column blockUuid (NOT the option text) - **SHOW/HIDE a full question** → questionUuid column - **SHOW/HIDE a single block (e.g. one option)** → blockUuid column - **REQUIRE** → questionUuid column - **JUMP TO PAGE** → page number column Each condition compares a field (left) to a value (right), e.g. ` > 100`. Don't apply math to the field: to check a calculated value (like price × qty > 100), store the result as a calc field first and use that. The right side is a literal, an option's blockUuid for choice fields, or another number or text field's questionUuid or calc field uuid, e.g. ` > `: - Choice fields (Dropdown, MultipleChoice): ` IS ` / `IS NOT ` - Choice fields: the left side is the questionUuid, never an option's blockUuid. 'Option X is selected' is ` IS ` (Checkboxes: `CONTAINS`) - Text/Email/Link/Phone fields: ` IS "literal text"` / `IS NOT "literal text"` - Empty check (any input field, never a calculated field): ` IS EMPTY` / `IS NOT EMPTY` - Number/Rating/LinearScale: ` > 5` (any of `> >= < <= = !=`) - Text matching: ` CONTAINS "text"` / `DOES NOT CONTAIN "text"` - Text matching: ` STARTS WITH "text"` / `ENDS WITH "text"` - Text matching: ` DOES NOT START WITH "text"` / `DOES NOT END WITH "text"` - Checkboxes/MultiSelect (arrays): ` IS ANY OF (,)` / `IS NOT ANY OF` / `IS EVERY OF` - Checkboxes/MultiSelect: do NOT use IS/IS NOT — use CONTAINS or IS ANY OF instead - Matrix: ` IS `; use CONTAINS / IS ANY OF when multiple selection is enabled - Date fields: ` IS BEFORE "2024-01-01"` / `IS AFTER "2024-01-01"` - Combine: ` AND ` or ` OR ` (parentheses required when mixing) - Highest score wins (quiz outcome counters): one JUMP rule per outcome that ANDs `>=` against every other counter, e.g. `WHEN >= AND >= THEN JUMP TO PAGE 3` - `SHOW ` / `HIDE ` (comma-separate for multiple) - `SHOW ` / `HIDE ` to target a single block within a question - `REQUIRE ` - `JUMP TO PAGE ` — jump to a specific page (use the page number from the ledger's page column). Check the Page flow section for current page order. - `JUMP TO END` — end the form early (jump to the default thank you page). If a custom thank you page exists, it will target that page instead. - `CALCULATE = ` — assign a formula expression to a calculated field. See below. - `DISABLE SUBMISSION` — hide the submit button so the form can't be submitted while the condition holds (eligibility gate). Takes no target. - Multiple actions: `SHOW , REQUIRE ` Group calc field writes that share a condition into one rule's THEN clause; only split into separate rules when the conditions differ (e.g., per-event accumulators). - **Target** (left of `=`): the UUID of a calculated field from a `CALCULATED_FIELDS` block. The ledger lists them in the properties column as `=()` — use the UUID. Create the block via create_blocks before writing CALCULATE rules. - **Expression** (right of `=`): `+ - * /` for NUMBER, `+` only for TEXT concat. Parens for precedence. Number and string literals allowed. Field refs are bare uuids – questionUuid for inputs, the calc field's own uuid (properties column) for cross-calc / self-reference. No blockUuid, no `{{ }}`, no functions. - **Choice fields**: a Dropdown/MultipleChoice/Checkboxes/MultiSelect questionUuid contributes its selected option's label as a number when the labels are numeric (e.g. options `"10"`, `"25"`); multi-value selections contribute the sum of the selected labels. A MATRIX_ROW uuid works the same with its selected column labels (e.g. columns `"1"` to `"5"`). Ranking fields are not numeric. - **Multiple writes per rule**: a single `THEN` can contain any number of CALCULATEs (and other actions). Comma-separated. - **Sequential evaluation**: CALCULATEs run top-to-bottom. Send writes to the same field in their intended execution order. The tool repairs cross-field order on the same page when it can, and reports unresolved dependencies. Never group CALCULATEs under one THEN just to control their order. - **Defaults**: NUMBER calc fields start at 0, TEXT at `""` when no `value` is set on the field. - **TEXT values are plain text**: no HTML or Markdown, the tool removes tags like `` or `
`. Put formatting in the TEXT block or email body that mentions the calc field, e.g. `{{}}`. Split a bold heading and a plain body into two calc fields. - **Constants on the field, not in rules**: For values that never change (e.g. `taxRate = 0.21`, `greeting = "Hi "`), set `value` on the calc field at creation time via create_blocks, not with a rule that writes the same literal whatever the answers. A literal under a condition that picks it is fine, e.g. one rule per option: `WHEN IS THEN CALCULATE = 25`. - **Calc fields are never empty** – they always carry the default (0 or `""`). IS [NOT] EMPTY on a calc field is rejected. To gate a calculation on user input completion, use IS NOT EMPTY on the INPUT field driving the calc (not on the calc itself). To check the calc value, use a numeric comparison (`> 0`, `!= 0`) for NUMBER or `IS` / `IS NOT` for TEXT — but only when the default specifically means "not yet answered" (e.g. quiz score), not when 0 / `""` is a legitimate result (e.g. an opt-out fee). - **Self-reference works** — the target can appear in its own expression. Use this for accumulators (quiz scoring, running totals) instead of creating per-question intermediate fields. - **No cycles between calc fields** — if rule A writes `` using ``, no other rule should write `` using ``. Grouping makes two CALCULATEs one rule, so don't put `` in the same THEN as a field another rule computes from ``. No order runs a cycle, so the tool reports it and leaves those rules where they are. Example patterns (replace `<...Uuid>` with real UUIDs from the ledger): WHEN IS NOT EMPTY THEN CALCULATE = * WHEN > 100 THEN CALCULATE = * 0.1 Plan dropdown with numeric price labels ("10", "25", "50") drives a total: WHEN IS NOT EMPTY THEN CALCULATE = * Add-on checkboxes with numeric price labels sum their checked options: WHEN IS NOT EMPTY THEN CALCULATE = + WHEN IS NOT EMPTY THEN CALCULATE = "Hello " + + " " + Multi-step under one condition — derive subtotal, tax, and total in a single rule: WHEN IS NOT EMPTY THEN CALCULATE = * , CALCULATE = * 0.21, CALCULATE = + Accumulator — one rule per event because the WHEN differs (quiz: +1 per correct answer): WHEN IS THEN CALCULATE = + 1 WHEN IS THEN CALCULATE = + 1 The tool handles these — do NOT do them manually: - SHOW auto-hides the target (isHidden: true). Do NOT call configure_blocks to hide it first. - REQUIRE auto-marks the target optional (isRequired: false). Do NOT call configure_blocks to unset it first. There is no if-else — do NOT add HIDE as the "else" for a SHOW rule. Logic rules are NOT if-else. All SHOW targets start hidden by default. When a SHOW condition is false, the target simply stays hidden — no HIDE needed. WRONG — adds useless HIDE actions: WHEN score <= 6 THEN SHOW feedback, HIDE review WHEN score >= 9 THEN SHOW review, HIDE feedback RIGHT — each rule only SHOWs its target: WHEN score <= 6 THEN SHOW feedback WHEN score >= 9 THEN SHOW review The HIDE in the wrong example is a no-op: - fields that are marked as SHOW are automatically hidden by default - fields that are marked as REQUIRE are automatically optional by default Match the action to the verb the user used. Don't invert by negating the condition. - User says "hide X when Y" → `WHEN THEN HIDE ` (target stays visible by default). - User says "show X when Y" → `WHEN THEN SHOW ` (target hidden by default, revealed when condition fires). User: "Hide the company name field when the role is Student" WRONG — inverted into SHOW + negated condition: WHEN role IS Professional THEN SHOW companyName WHEN role IS Academic THEN SHOW companyName RIGHT — direct HIDE matching the user's verb: WHEN role IS Student THEN HIDE companyName Follow the user's explicit destinations. Do not infer extra routes from field or option labels. When only blank answers should jump, add IS EMPTY only; selected answers keep their default path, even if an option label suggests skipping. A page jump — JUMP TO PAGE or JUMP TO END — is an override on top of the default linear page order: it only fires when its WHEN condition is true. Before adding one, decide whether skipping the gating field is a mistake or a valid choice: - Branch routing / eligibility screen-out — every respondent must reach a specific page based on their answer. Make the gating field required (set isRequired via configure_blocks); otherwise anyone who skips it never matches the jump and falls through to the wrong linear page (or, for a skipped JUMP TO END, the form never exits and keeps collecting). Don't rely on the linear fall-through to carry a branch that should have jumped. - Optional opt-out / "skip ahead" — skipping is itself a valid choice and leaving the field blank is meant to continue to the next page. Leave the field optional; don't force it required. When in doubt, treat it as branch routing and make the field required — only leave it optional when skipping is clearly an intended opt-out, a rule routes blank answers, or a conditional REQUIRE rule controls it. Branch routing — route to the "Press" page when topic IS Press, and every respondent must reach their team's page: WRONG — topic is optional, so respondents who skip it fall through to the next linear page: WHEN IS THEN JUMP TO PAGE 8 RIGHT — make required (isRequired via configure_blocks) so the jump always fires. Optional opt-out — "Skip the remaining questions?" jumps to the end when chosen, and leaving it blank is meant to continue: WHEN IS THEN JUMP TO END Leave optional — skipping is intentional, so falling through to the next page is correct. ```ts mcp__Tally__apply_logic(args: { // The form to act on: its id, or a share, edit or embed link to it. tools.description:
Soft-stop every member of a batch or pipeline in one call. Flips
JobStatus to "Stopped" on all batch children, all pipeline stages,
and the pipeline parent row (if one exists). Doesn't delete rows
or outputs.

Use this when the user wants to stop a batch or pipeline as a
unit. Don't call cancelJob N times — this fans out server-side
via the Batch-index GSI in one round-trip.

Pipeline support is for LEGACY pipelines only: their stages carry
`Batch=<pipeline_name>`, so a pipeline name resolves through the
same index a batch name does, and the parent row (Type='pipelines')
is looked up separately via JobName-index and cancelled too.

This does NOT stop a run created by submitPipeline. Those are
Type='pipeline-run', a deliberately different job type that neither
index reaches — use stopPipelineRun(runId) for them.

Only cancels jobs in "In Queue", "Running", or "Pending" status —
already-terminal jobs are skipped.



**Responses:**

- **200** (Success): Batch cancellation summary
  - Content-Type: `application/json`

  - **Response Properties:**

    - **cancelledCount**: Number of rows successfully flipped to Stopped.

    - **totalChildren**: Total batch/pipeline children found (any status).

    - **cancellableChildren**: Children in In Queue / Running / Pending — the subset eligible for cancel.

    - **parentCancelled**: True if a pipeline parent row was found and cancelled too.

  - **Example:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Cancelled 12 jobs in batch \"my-batch\"",
  "batchName": "string"
}
```

- **400**: batchName missing or invalid

- **401**: Unauthorized

- **404**: No batch or pipeline with that name found for this user

```ts
mcp__Tamarind_Bio__cancelBatch(args: {
// Batch or pipeline name — same value used as `batchName` for submit-batch or `pipeline_name` for buildPipeline.
batchName: string,
}): Promise<{
batchName?: string,
// Children in In Queue / Running / Pending — the subset eligible for cancel.
cancellableChildren?: integer,
// Number of rows successfully flipped to Stopped.
cancelledCount?: integer,
message?: string,
// True if a pipeline parent row was found and cancelled too.
parentCancelled?: boolean,
success?: boolean,
// Total batch/pipeline children found (any status).
```

tools.description:
Soft-stop a job — flips JobStatus to "Stopped" (same value the
website cancel button writes) without deleting the row or outputs.
Only works on jobs in "In Queue", "Running", or "Pending" status;
jobs already in a terminal state are rejected with 400.

Accepts either `jobName` (preferred — looked up via JobName-index
GSI server-side, no need for callers to know the Id) or `jobId`
(the DDB Id, if already known). At least one is required.

Different from deleteJob, which permanently removes the row +
outputs. cancelJob preserves both.



**Responses:**

- **200** (Success): Job cancelled
  - Content-Type: `application/json`

  - **Response Properties:**

  - **Example:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Job cancelled successfully",
  "jobId": "string"
}
```

- **400**: Job not in a cancellable state (already Completed / Failed / Cancelled)

- **401**: Unauthorized

- **403**: Access denied (job belongs to another user)

- **404**: Job not found

```ts
mcp__Tamarind_Bio__cancelJob(args: {
// DDB row Id (alternative input, use if already known).
jobId?: string,
// Name of the job to cancel (preferred input).
jobName?: string,
```

tools.name: mcp__Tamarind_Bio__createMolecules
tools.description:
Create a NAMED, reusable molecule group and return its `groupId` — the id you
bind as {"group": "<groupId>"} in submitPipeline/validatePipeline.

You do not need this to run a pipeline once: a binding takes raw values inline
({"sequences": [...]}, {"smiles": [...]}) and the server mints a throwaway group.
Use this when you want a cohort you can name, find again with
listMoleculeGroups(), and bind across MANY runs — or when you want per-molecule
metadata that searchMolecules() can later filter and rank on.

CSVs: read the file yourself and pass one object per row — the name column as
"name", the sequence/SMILES column as the chain, and every other column inside
"metadata". Mapping the columns deliberately beats a server-side guess, and
metadata is exactly what searchMolecules() filters on afterwards.

TEXT CHAINS ONLY — sequences and SMILES. Use importMoleculeFile for structures (pdbIds for
PDB entries, or uploaded PDB/CIF/ZIP files) and SDF ligands; it waits until they are ingested.

LIGANDS: use the {"smiles": "..."} shorthand and the kind is declared for you. If
you instead spell a ligand out under "entity", you MUST say so via `chainMapping`,
e.g. entity {"A": "MKT...", "B": "CCO"} with chainMapping {"B": {"type":
"small_molecule"}} — the server cannot infer it, because a SMILES made only of
sequence letters (CCO is ethanol AND a tripeptide) reads as a protein and then
fails validation. A per-molecule "type": "small_molecule" does NOT do this; only
`chainMapping` does. Nucleic acids are the other way round: give the MOLECULE
"type": "nucleic_acid" and its chains follow.

This waits for the upload to finish ingesting before returning, so a `status:
"ingested"` group is ready to bind. If the wait runs out you still get the
groupId, but with `status: "pending"` — do NOT bind that one yet. A partly
ingested group passes validation (only a completely EMPTY one is rejected) and
would run over however many molecules had landed by then.

Chain labels must be 1-4 UPPERCASE letters or digits ("A", "H", "L", "AB1").
Descriptive labels like {"heavy": ..., "light": ...} are rejected — put the
description in "name" and use {"H": ..., "L": ...} for the chains.

METADATA IS SHARED BY IDENTICAL MOLECULES, and identical means identical CHAINS —
the same sequence uploaded into two groups is ONE molecule with ONE set of
annotations, org-wide. Importing that sequence again with different `metadata`
OVERWRITES the earlier values (per key), and re-importing it with different `tags`
silently keeps the ORIGINAL tags. So a key like {"round": 2} does not mean "round 2
in this group" — if you need per-cohort annotations, use a key that names the
cohort, or keep the distinction in the group name and tags.

Args:
    name: Name for the group, 1-200 characters. Required.
    molecules: 1-1000 molecules. A string is one chain; an object takes
        {"entity": {"A": "...", "B": "..."}} (or {"sequence"}/{"smiles"} for a
        single chain) plus optional "name", "type", "metadata", "tags". Any OTHER
        key is rejected — annotations go inside "metadata", not beside it.
        Example: [{"name": "d1", "sequence": "MKT...", "metadata": {"round": 2}}]
    type: Molecule kind for the GROUP — one of protein, antibody, peptide, enzyme,
        small_molecule, nucleic_acid, small_molecule_binding_protein.
        Per-molecule types are inferred; omit unless the group is uniform and
        you want it labelled.
    tags: Tags for the group.
    chainMapping: Per-CHAIN-LABEL declarations, {label: {"type": "protein" |
        "small_molecule", "tags": ["heavy"|"light"|"lead"]}}. Needed only when you
        spell a ligand out under "entity" — the {"smiles": ...} shorthand fills
        this in for you. Keyed by label and applied to the WHOLE upload, so a
        label means the same thing in every molecule of one call.
    waitSeconds: How long to wait for ingestion, 0-200 (default 60). Pass 0 to
        return as soon as the upload is accepted.

Returns:
    JSON: { groupId, name, moleculeCount, moleculeIds, status, importId }.
    `status` is "ingested" (ready to bind), "pending" (still ingesting — the
    group is real but NOT yet safe to bind; poll listMoleculeGroups until that
    group's `status` is "ready") or "failed". `moleculeCount` counts the entries
    you SENT and `moleculeIds` has one id per entry, in order; identical entries
    share one id, and `distinctMoleculeCount` appears when the group will
    therefore hold fewer molecules than you sent.

```ts
mcp__Tamarind_Bio__createMolecules(args: {
// Name
name: string,
// Molecules
molecules: any[],
// Type
type?: string | null, // default: null
// Tags
tags?: any[] | null, // default: null
// Chainmapping
chainMapping?: { [key: string]: any } | null, // default: null
// Waitseconds
waitSeconds?: number | null, // default: null
}): Promise<// _WrappedResult
{
// Result
result: string,
}>;
```

tools.description:
Deploy your organization's own code as a Tamarind tool: create it if needed,
upload the source, build an image, run a build as a test, and publish it.

Calling this again with new source IS the update path — there is no separate
update call. Identical source returns `unchanged` without rebuilding, and a
code-only change returns `reuse_image` and skips the image build.

Exactly one mode per call:

- BUILD — pass `files` (and `binaryFiles`). Creates the tool if it does not
  exist, uploads, and starts a build.
- TEST — pass `testVersion` (and `testSettings`) to run a Complete build as a job in
  the tool's Test history on the website, without publishing it. It runs the tool,
  so it uses compute. An identical test runs once; calling again reports that run.
- PUBLISH — pass `publishVersion` alone to promote an already-built version.
  This is also how you roll back: publish an older completed version.
- CANCEL — pass `cancelVersion` alone to stop an in-progress build.

SOURCE FORMAT. `files` maps archive-relative path to text content;
`Dockerfile`, `run.sh`, and `config.json` belong at its ROOT. Binary members
go in `binaryFiles` as base64. At runtime the working directory is `/app`,
scalar inputs arrive as environment variables named after `config.json`'s
`inputs[]`, file inputs arrive as absolute paths under `/app/inputs/` (which
is writable, so a tool whose code wants its input at a fixed path can stage
it there), results must be
written to `/app/out/`, and THE CONTAINER HAS NO NETWORK — bake packages and
model weights into the image in the Dockerfile, which does have network. Bake
them OUTSIDE `/app` (use `/opt/<tool>/`): the uploaded source replaces `/app`
at runtime, so anything the Dockerfile fetches there is missing when the job
runs, even though it passed its build-time checksum.

PUBLISHING IS ORGANIZATION-WIDE. It changes what every member gets when they
submit this tool, so only pass `publish=True` (or `publishVersion`) once the
user has authorized that exact promotion.

VERSION HANDLES. Every result that names a version also returns its
`versionHandle`, such as "v3@3f9a2c1b7d0e4a5c": the version name pinned to the
exact build. Pass the handle — not the bare name — to publishVersion,
testVersion and cancelVersion. A tool deleted and recreated under the same name
has its own "v3"; a handle refuses it (412 `version_handle_stale`, nothing
changed), so an approval of one build can never promote another. A bare name
such as "v3" still works and means whatever v3 the tool has when the call runs.

Args:
    name: Organization-unique tool name.
    files: {"Dockerfile": "...", "run.sh": "...", "config.json": "..."} — text content.
    binaryFiles: Same shape for binary members, base64-encoded.
    displayName: Human-readable name. Used only when the tool is created.
    description: One-line description. Used only when the tool is created.
    publish: Publish the new version once it builds. Requires waitSeconds > 0, so it
        only lands when no image build was needed. Otherwise publish separately with
        publishVersion once the build is Complete.
    waitSeconds: Poll the build for up to this long (max 45 — MCP clients abort longer
        calls). 0 returns immediately. An image build takes minutes, so expect to poll
        with getCustomTool rather than wait here.
    validateOnly: Check and hash the archive without creating or uploading anything.
    publishVersion: PUBLISH mode — the version to promote: its `versionHandle` such as
        "v3@3f9a2c1b7d0e4a5c" from build or getCustomTool (pins the reviewed build), or a
        bare name such as "v3" (the current v3).
    cancelVersion: CANCEL mode — the version to cancel, by handle or name, as above.
    testVersion: TEST mode — the version to run, by handle or name, as above.
    testSettings: TEST mode — the run's inputs, named as in config.json `inputs[]`.
    projectTag: TEST mode — the organization project id to file the run under (listProjects).
        Orgs that require a project tag refuse a test without one.
    idempotencyKey: Optional stable key for retrying the same build after an ambiguous response.
        Reuse only for the same source and runtime request; a different request conflicts.
        In TEST mode, a new key runs an identical test again.
    expectNew: Refuse to update an existing tool. Pass True whenever you believe the name
        is free — a listing is a snapshot, and another member can claim the name between
        your check and this call.

Returns:
    JSON. Build: {"action": "build"|"reuse_image"|"unchanged", "version",
    "versionHandle", "sourceDigest", "created", "published"}; the version's name
    ("v3") is `version.version`. If the tool was just created and a later step failed,
    the error carries `created: true` — the tool now exists as a Draft, so retry
    without expectNew. `staleAfterCreate: true` instead means the new tool was changed
    or replaced before the build (412): nothing was built, and retrying without
    expectNew could update someone else's tool — follow its hint. `action: "unchanged"` means identical source already
    has a version and nothing was rebuilt. Poll with getCustomTool until the version
    is terminal. Test: {"action": "test", "version", "job": {"jobName", "id", "status"}};
    follow the job with getJobs(jobName=...). `alreadySubmitted` means this exact test
    already ran and nothing new started.

```ts
mcp__Tamarind_Bio__deployCustomTool(args: {
// Binaryfiles
binaryFiles?: { [key: string]: any }, // default: null
// Cancelversion
cancelVersion?: string, // default: null
// Description
description?: string, // default: null
// Displayname
displayName?: string, // default: null
// Expectnew
expectNew?: boolean, // default: false
// Files
files?: { [key: string]: any }, // default: null
// Idempotencykey
idempotencyKey?: string, // default: null
// Name
name: string,
// Projecttag

// Publish

// Publishversion
publishVersion?: string, // default: null
// Testsettings
testSettings?: { [key: string]: any }, // default: null
// Testversion
testVersion?: string, // default: null
// Validateonly
validateOnly?: boolean, // default: false
// Waitseconds
waitSeconds?: integer, // default: 0
}): Promise<// _WrappedResult
{
// Result
```

tools.description:
Price a pipeline run WITHOUT running it. This spends NOTHING — no run, no jobs,
no saved template, no molecule group is created. Call it before submitPipeline to
check what a run will cost.

Takes exactly the arguments submitPipeline prices: the graph (`pipeline` or
`templateId`+`version`), `bindings`, `settings` and `name`, and prices exactly what
submitPipeline would run — the same version (explicit `version`, else
published-then-latest) and the same molecules, raw-value bindings included.
submitPipeline's `runName`, `project` and `idempotencyKey` only name and tag the
run, so they are not taken here.

`totalWeightedHours` is the number the platform's budget gate enforces when the
run is submitted, so compare THAT against a budget. `perNode` breaks it down by
pipeline node (molecules in/out, jobs, weightedHours each), and `assumptions`
says what the figure takes for granted — chiefly that every molecule passes every
filter, so a filtered pipeline usually costs less than quoted.

`estimateFailed: true` means there is NO quote: the platform could not price
the run, and the totals are not a cost (in particular, not a zero cost). Do not
read a failed estimate as "free" or as within budget.

If `estimateUnavailable` comes back, the estimator could not be reached and the
run was NOT priced — retry once or twice. Any other error means the run was
refused (an unknown template, a bad setting override, ...); call validatePipeline
on the same graph and bindings for per-node diagnostics.

Args:
    name: A name for the pipeline/run. Required.
    bindings: One entry per input node, keyed by the input node's id, exactly
        as for submitPipeline: {"group": "<groupId>"} for an existing molecule
        group, or raw values — {"sequences": [...]}, {"smiles": [...]},
        {"pdbs": ["<uploadedPath>"]}, {"sdfs": [...]} — which are priced as the
        group submitPipeline would create from them (none is created here). A
        file input takes {"file": "<path>"}. "residuesByChain" and
        "chainMapping" go in the binding as for submitPipeline.
    pipeline: INLINE mode — a full pipeline IR. Mutually exclusive with templateId.
    templateId: REFERENCE mode — an existing template.
    version: REFERENCE mode only — a version handle like "v2". Omit for
        published-then-latest, the version submitPipeline would run.
    settings: Per-node overrides {nodeId: {settingKey: value}}; in REFERENCE
        mode limited to the template's editable settings.

Returns:
    JSON: { totalWeightedHours, totalJobs, estimateFailed,
    perNode: [{node, tool, label, molecules, outputMolecules, jobs, weightedHours}],
    assumptions: [str] }.

will cost — BEFORE submitting anything. Use it to plan a run, compare tools,
warn the user about a slow or expensive job, or budget a design loop.

so it matches what submitting this job would quote. No job is created.

- numJobs: how many jobs these settings expand into (e.g. multiple sequences).
- weightedHours: total compute-hour cost across the whole submission (the

tools.name: mcp__Tamarind_Bio__getAvailableTools
tools.description:
Get list of all available tools/job types in the Tamarind platform.

Use this tool BEFORE submitting jobs to discover what tools are available.
For only the tools you can finetune (train a model with), use
getAvailableModels.
The catalog is large, so FILTER rather than listing everything: narrow by
`modality` (the molecule type) and/or `function` (what the tool does), or by
a free-text `search`. Call listModalities() and listTags() first to see the
valid values (with descriptions) for those two filters.

Args:
    modality: Filter by molecule type (e.g. "antibody", "protein", "peptide",
              "small-molecule", "nucleic-acid"). See listModalities().
    function: Filter by what the tool does (e.g. "structure-prediction",
              "binder-design", "protein-ligand-docking"). See listTags().
    category: Deprecated alias for `modality` (still honored).
    tag: Deprecated alias for `function` (still honored).
    search: Search in tool name or description
    custom: If true, return only custom tools; if false/None, return standard tools from database

The catalog drifts as tools are added/removed, so don't guess values — every
response includes the exact live `availableCategories` and `availableTags`
(a.k.a. modalities and functions) computed from the current catalog, or call
listModalities()/listTags() for the same vocabulary with descriptions.

Returns:
    JSON with `tools` (name, displayName, categories, outputTypes[, tags,
    description]), plus `availableCategories` and `availableTags` — the live
    facet lists to filter against.

    `outputTypes` is what a tool declares it produces — molecular (pdb, sequence,
    sdf, smiles) and otherwise (csv, score, cif, ...). A few tools use compound
    values such as "pdb-list" or "sequence-list", so match by CONTAINMENT, not
    equality. Use it to plan a multi-step run: a molecular type here must cover
    what the next tool takes as input. It is
    OMITTED when the tool declares nothing, which means UNKNOWN — not "produces
    nothing", so confirm with getJobSchema rather than ruling the tool out. A type
    here is also not proof the tool GENERATED it: a scorer can echo its input
    sequence alongside the scores. getJobSchema's `taskType` is what distinguishes
    generating from scoring, along with the full result contract — the results CSV
    and its columns, i.e. the metric names to filter or rank on.

Examples:
    - Find antibody tools: modality="antibody"
    - Find structure prediction tools: function="structure-prediction"
    - Narrow to antibody structure prediction: modality="antibody", function="structure-prediction"
    - Search for AlphaFold variants: search="alphafold"
    - Find custom tools: custom=true

Inspect your organization's custom tools, or poll one tool's build.

Call with no `name` to list the custom tools your organization owns, including
Drafts that are not yet published. Published custom tools are also visible as
ordinary tools through getAvailableTools(custom=True), with their submit

this is the polling call after deployCustomTool. Add `listVersions=True` to get
the tool's version history instead, newest first; that is where a rollback
target comes from, because publishing an older Complete version IS the rollback. Stop when the version's

terminal build can carry a structured `error`.

Build-log cursors stay live while a build runs: carry `logs.nextCursor` into
the next poll and sleep between polls. A REPEATED non-null cursor means "no new
logs yet", not "drain another page immediately". It goes null once the terminal
log stream is exhausted.

    name: The tool's name. Omit to list every custom tool in the organization.
    version: A `versionHandle` such as "v3@3f9a2c1b7d0e4a5c" (refused if the tool was

    listVersions: With `name`, list that tool's versions newest-first instead of
        reading one. This is how you find a rollback target — an older version
        whose status is Complete. Paginate with `cursor`.
    logCursor: `logs.nextCursor` from the previous poll, to resume the log stream.
    cursor: Listing mode only — `nextCursor` from the previous page. Follow it until null.

mcp__Tamarind_Bio__getJobFile
tools.description:
Read or download any of your files: job outputs AND your uploaded files.
ONE call, ONE link, however many files.

Each entry in `files` is one of:
  - a job's output, as "jobName/fileName": the `s3Path` values
    listJobFiles() returns, passed straight through
  - one of your uploaded files, by its name exactly as getFiles() lists it
    (no "/"), e.g. "solubility.csv"

    getJobFile(files=["my-job/results.csv"])               # one job file
    getJobFile(files=["solubility.csv"])                   # one upload
    getJobFile(files=["job-a/x.csv", "job-b/y.csv"])       # any number
    getJobFile(files=["solubility.csv", "my-job/x.csv"])   # any mix

Use listJobFiles() (job outputs) or getFiles() (uploads) first to see what
exists — this tool does not search, it fetches exactly what you name. A
whole batch is therefore two calls:

    found = listJobFiles("my-batch-*", "*-scores.csv")["files"]
    getJobFile(files=[f["s3Path"] for f in found])

Do NOT call this once per file. One call takes the whole set; a loop is what
makes a batch download slow and floods the context.

You get back a short-lived `downloadUrl` plus a `files` manifest of what it
covers. Fetch everything with the single command in `instructions`:

    curl -fsS -o results.zip "<downloadUrl>" && unzip -o results.zip -d <DEST>

One file streams raw; many files stream as a zip. As a convenience, a SINGLE
text file under 256 KB comes back as `content` inline instead, so reading one
log or CSV stays a single call. Pass maxSizeMB=0 to decline that and always
get a `downloadUrl` — do that when you want the file ON DISK, since a 256 KB
log inlined is ~65K tokens of context spent on bytes you meant to save.

When you want only PART of what a glob matches — "batch 28 and onwards",
"the ten largest" — filter the listJobFiles() result in code and pass the
paths you kept.

IF curl FAILS with HTTP 403 from a proxy (not from Tamarind), "could not resolve
host", "network unreachable" or HTTP 000, your MCP client's sandbox is blocking
outbound network. The MCP tools
still work (they go through the client, not your shell) — only curl needs
egress to the downloadUrl's host, which is named in `instructions`. Tell the
USER to allow that host (Claude Desktop/Claude.ai: Settings -> Capabilities
-> "Allow network egress"; other clients: their network allowlist), then
re-run the curl. If egress can't be enabled, read the files you need one at a
time inline with maxSizeMB (up to 50 MB each) instead.

Args:
    files: List of "jobName/fileName" paths — the `s3Path` values from
           listJobFiles(), e.g. ["my-job/results.csv"] — and/or uploaded
           file names as getFiles() lists them, e.g. ["solubility.csv"]
    maxSizeMB: How many megabytes a SINGLE file may ride the tool channel
               as inline `content`. Default 256 KB. RAISE it (max 50) when
               your shell has no network access and curl is unavailable;
               set it to 0 to switch inlining OFF and always receive a
               `downloadUrl`, which is what you want when the file is
               headed for disk.
    jobName, fileName: DEPRECATED single-file form, equivalent to
               files=["<jobName>/<fileName>"]. Still accepted so clients
               holding a cached tool list keep working. Prefer `files`.

Returns:
    JSON: {"downloadUrl", "downloadType", "count", "totalBytes",
           "expiresInSeconds", "instructions", "files": [{"s3Path",
           "size"}]} — or, for one small text file,
    {"content", "jobName", "fileName", "s3Path", "size", ...}
    (an upload's "jobName" is null and its "s3Path" is its name)

    CHECK "error" FIRST here too: a refusal (unknown or unauthorised job, a
    path that does not exist, a selection over the limits) returns
    {"error", "hint", ...} with NO "downloadUrl", "count" or "files".

    For a zip, "zipLayout" says how the members are named: "flat" when every
    file's path WITHIN its job is unique — any subdirectories are kept, only
    the "<jobName>/" prefix is dropped — otherwise every member is nested
    under "<jobName>/". Uploads always sit at the top level. Unzip into a
    directory (-d) rather than the cwd either way.

Security:
    - Every entry is checked for path traversal, and matching is confined to
      your own files
    - Every job named is checked against the backend before anything is
      served — owning the prefix is not by itself authorization
    - An upload is read only from the top level of your own files

```ts
fileName?: string, // default: null

files?: any[], // default: null

jobName?: string, // default: null

maxSizeMB?: integer, // default: null
```

tools.description:
Get the detailed parameter schema for a specific job type.

Checks both standard tools (DynamoDB) and custom tools (API) to find the schema.
Returns the complete schema including all parameter definitions with their types,
descriptions, validation rules, and metadata.

Args:
    jobType: Job type name (e.g., "proteinmpnn", "alphafold", "rfdiffusion", or custom tool name)

Returns:
    Complete JSON schema for the job type including:
    - parameters: full parameter definitions (name, type, description, required, etc.)
    - displayName: human-readable tool name
    - description: tool description
    - categories: tool categories
    - tags: tool tags
    - outputTypes: what this tool declares it produces — molecular (pdb, sequence,
      sdf, smiles) and otherwise (csv, score, cif, ...); a few are compound, like
      "pdb-list", so match by CONTAINMENT. Chain on the molecular ones: they must
      cover what the next tool takes as input. Absent means the tool declares
      nothing (UNKNOWN), not that it produces nothing.
    - outputs: what the results look like — `taskType` (`generate` vs `score` is
      what tells you whether the tool creates a molecule or just annotates one),
      `produces` (molecular representations the output carries — as a column of the
      result table OR as a file written alongside it — INCLUDING any echoed from the
      input, so a scorer can list one), `mainCSV`, and
      `columns` (name, type, description, units). The column names are the metrics
      to filter or rank results on. Absent when the tool declares no contract.

      For a tool whose output depends on the task it runs, `outputs.byTask` gives
      the per-task contract and is AUTHORITATIVE for the task you set — read it
      instead of the scalar fields, which summarize across tasks and are NOT
      guaranteed to describe the task selector's default. Each entry is complete
      (a task inherits the top-level `mainCSV`/`taskType` when it doesn't
      redeclare them) and carries `generates`: what that task creates fresh, which
      is empty for a scoring task whose table still echoes its input. A column
      carrying a `tasks` list appears only in those tasks; an UNTAGGED column is
      simply not task-gated in the declaration, which does not promise every task
      fills it — read `generates` for what a task actually produces.
      `outputs.byTaskNote` restates this on the response.
    - custom: true if this is a custom tool (only present for custom tools)

Examples:
    - getJobSchema("alphafold")
    - getJobSchema("proteinmpnn")
    - getJobSchema("protein_properties_wmo6g")  # custom tool

```ts
jobType: string,
```

tools.name: mcp__Tamarind_Bio__getPipelineRunResults
tools.description:
Read a pipeline run's OUTPUTS — the molecules each step produced, with their
scores — rather than just its status.

Returns every step's molecules, with their scores — which is what you rank and
compare on. A step's molecules come from one of two API resources, and WHERE
the scores sit differs between them, so read whichever shape you get:

  * group molecules — id in `id`, scores under `metadata`;
  * the step's own outputs — id in `complexId`, scores at top level in
    `scores`.

Passed through as they come rather than reshaped here, so the fields match what
the docs for each resource say. A step with an `outputGroup` is normally read
from the group, but falls back to its own outputs when the group returns
nothing — so do not assume a step's shape from whether `outputGroup` is set.

`outputGroup` is the molecules group a step MINTED, and a step that produced
plenty may still have none: one that enriches its inputs in place (scoring,
structure prediction) leaves its molecules in the group they came from, and a
filter step's survivors exist only as step outputs. Those steps report
`outputGroup: null` and their molecules are read from the step itself, so a
null group no longer means "nothing here".

Results appear per step as it finishes, so this is useful before the whole
run is complete. A step reports an empty `molecules` list when it genuinely
has not produced anything yet.

To page through a step that produced more than `limit` molecules: call again with
`node` set to that step and `cursor` set to its `nextCursor`.

Args:
    runId: The run id.
    node: Only this step's outputs — the `nodeId` value from getPipelineRun's
        `nodeRuns`. Omit for every step that has produced output.
    limit: Molecules per step, 1-100 (default 25). Keep it small — molecules
        carry their sequences, files and full score history.
    cursor: A `nextCursor` from a previous call, to fetch the next page. Requires
        `node`, since a cursor belongs to one step's group.

Returns:
    JSON: { runId, status, steps: [{node, label, status, outputGroup,
    molecules[], nextCursor, error?}] }.

tools.name: mcp__Tamarind_Bio__getPipelineSchema
tools.description:
Get the pipeline IR schema and the full authoring guide. Call this BEFORE
writing a `pipeline` graph for submitPipeline/validatePipeline — the IR has
rules that are not guessable, and authoring blind reliably produces graphs
the API rejects.

Returns the complete, uncompressed JSON Schema plus the prose guide. Both are
fetched live from the app host, so they always match the deployed validator.

The guide covers, among other things: the four node kinds; that there is NO
edge list (topology lives inside each node's `inputs`); that every molecule
`user_input` needs a reference group; that a `filter` node must either set
`intersect: true` or carry at least one rule; and that residue selections are
supplied per-run in the BINDING (`residuesByChain`), never as a node setting.

Returns:
    JSON: { schemaUrl, guideUrl, schema, guide }. On failure, `error` plus
    the two URLs so you can read them another way.

```ts

{
// Result
result: string,
}>;
```

tools.name: mcp__Tamarind_Bio__getPipelineTemplate
tools.description:
Get one pipeline template: its graph, its bindable inputs, and its versions.

The `inputs` array is the important part — it is the manifest of what you
must pass as `bindings` to submitPipeline/validatePipeline. Each entry gives
the input node id to key the binding by, whether it takes molecules or a
file, the molecule type it expects, its reference chain labels, and any
`residueFields`. A non-empty `residueFields` means the run MAY take a
`residuesByChain` selection in this input's binding — it does NOT mean one is
required. This said REQUIRES, and it is not true: production runs of the
rfdiffusion, bindcraft and antibody-boltzgen templates whose manifests declare
residueFields finished with no `residuesByChain` at all, and the entries carry no
per-field `required` flag to tell the two apart. Believing it forces a choice
between refusing a runnable template and inventing a selection — and an invented
one is not a no-op: it reaches the tool as designed residues / binder hotspots /
a binding site, constraining the design to the wrong residues and spending GPU on
scientifically wrong output that still looks successful.

Do not guess. Call validatePipeline with the bindings you have: if a selection is
genuinely required, it comes back as `required-field-unset` naming the field. Note
also that `targetsChains` is empty on some entries and names a chain outside the
input's own `chains` on others (a de-novo chain the graph creates), so it is not
always a usable key for `residuesByChain`.

Args:
    templateId: The template id (from listPipelineTemplates).
    version: A version handle like "v2". Omit for the version a default run
        would use (published, else latest).

Returns:
    JSON PublicTemplate: { id, name, description, isPublished,
    publishedVersion, version, pipeline (the IR), inputs[], versions[],
    createdAt, updatedAt }.

```ts

templateId: string,
```

tools.description:
Import structures into a molecule group, a new one named `name` or the existing `groupId`,
and by default wait until they are ingested, so one call usually returns moleculeIds ready for Jobs.

Two sources; pass exactly one:

- pdbIds: PUBLIC STRUCTURES, NO UPLOAD. Up to 1,000 PDB IDs (e.g. ["1BRS", "2PTC"]); each is
  fetched by the platform from our internal PDB mirror as the deposited mmCIF and imported as
  its own structure, named by its id. A repeat is imported once. An id that can't be imported
  (not in the mirror, e.g. a very new entry, or too large) comes back with an `error` and the
  rest go on. Prefer this over downloading and uploading files for anything in the PDB.
- fileName: YOUR OWN FILES, the bare filename returned by uploadFile (nested storage paths are
  not accepted). .pdb, .ent, .cif or .mmcif for a structure with a protein or nucleic acid
  chain; .sdf for ligands, which keeps their 3D coordinates (a PDB holding only a ligand
  imports nothing, so send that ligand as an SDF). It also prepares a PDB for Protein
  Solubilization.

MANY FILES: zip them and import the .zip. One upload and one import put every .pdb, .cif and
.mmcif inside it (folders are fine) into one group, a molecule per distinct structure; other
entries (.ent, .sdf, README) are skipped and listed under skippedEntries. A ZIP is at most 16 MiB,
which is roughly 300 typical PDB files (it may hold up to 30,000 entries, and members up to
64 MiB uncompressed). A larger set goes in several ZIPs into the same `groupId`, imported in
parallel. For structures that are in the PDB, pdbIds is faster: nothing to upload.
structureCount is how many structures the ZIP holds; fewer molecules can come back, since
structures with identical chains share one molecule (into an existing group, moleculeIds can
include molecules it already held). Imports run in parallel, so several calls into one group can
be in flight.

GROUP TYPE: a new group's type follows its structures: protein, nucleic_acid, or no type when
they hold both (no type takes any chain). An existing protein group can't take nucleic-acid
chains (or the reverse): import those into a new group.

WAITING: the call waits up to waitSeconds (default 60, at most 300; 0 returns right after the
import starts) for ingestion, about 10 seconds per structure. Starting the imports counts toward
it, and a call never runs past about 270 s: 1,000 PDB IDs take about 2 minutes just to start. It returns status=ingested with
moleculeIds, or failed with error {code, message} saying what to fix. If time runs out it
returns the import ids still pending: poll getMoleculeImport for those. Use moleculeIds as
pickerComplex complexId values together with groupId; omit settings.pdbFile.

Args:
    fileName: The bare filename returned by uploadFile (.pdb, .ent, .cif, .mmcif, .sdf or .zip).
    name: Name of the new group. Required unless groupId is given.
    groupId: Add the structures to this existing group instead of creating one.
    pdbIds: PDB IDs to import instead of a file, up to 1,000.
    waitSeconds: How long to wait for ingestion, 0 to 300 (default 60).

```ts
// Groupid

// Name

// Pdbids
```

tools.name: mcp__Tamarind_Bio__listAssayTargets
tools.description:
Search a lab's target list to find a target's `id` for a binding assay. Read-only.

Put the id in the order's `settings`. The field depends on the lab:
  - Adaptyv: `targetId` (one id).
  - A-Alpha Bio: `targetIds` (a list of ids).
  - Ginkgo: `targetAntigen` (one id, which for Ginkgo is the antigen's name).
The assay type's `targetsProvider` (from listAssayTypes) says which lab's list
to search.

Needs Assay Portal access: 403 `wetlab_access_required` otherwise. A 502
`targets_unavailable` means the lab's list could not be loaded just now; try
again shortly.



**Query Parameters:**

- **provider** (Required): The lab whose targets to search, from the assay type's `targetsProvider`.

- **search**: Text to look for in a target's id, name, aliases or UniProt id, e.g. "PD-L1"
or "Q9NZQ7". Not case-sensitive. Searching is much better than paging
through the whole list.


- **limit**: How many targets to return, up to 500.


**Responses:**

- **200** (Success): The targets that match
  - Content-Type: `application/json`

  - **Response Properties:**

    - **total**: How many targets matched in all.

    - **truncated**: True when more targets matched than were returned. Narrow `search` or raise `limit`.

```json
  "targets": [

      "name": "string",
      "uniprotId": "string"

  "total": 1
```

- **502**: The lab's target list could not be loaded just now (`targets_unavailable`)

tools.name: mcp__Tamarind_Bio__listAssayTypes
tools.description:
List the wet-lab assays you can order through Tamarind's Assay Portal, such as
binding affinity, binding screens, expression, thermostability and
developability. Partner labs (Adaptyv, Ginkgo, A-Alpha Bio) run them on your
sequences. Read-only.

Start every assay order here. Each assay type gives:
  - `assayType`: the id to order with.
  - `modalities`: whether it takes antibodies, proteins or both. Send
    `modality` on the order when it takes both.
  - `minSequences` / `maxSequences`.
  - `settings`: what the order's `settings` object takes: a name, a type,
    whether it is required, the `options` to choose from when there is a
    fixed set, the `default`, and `list` when it takes an array.

the order tools answer 403 `wetlab_access_required`. The user can ask for

  2. listAssayTargets: when the type has a `targetsProvider`.

tools.description:
List job output files — across ONE job or MANY, without downloading anything.

Answers "what exists?" cheaply: names, sizes and `s3Path` only — no file
contents and no download URLs. This is always the first step, because
getJobFile does not search; it fetches the paths you hand it.

    listJobFiles("my-job")                      # every file in one job
    listJobFiles("my-job", "*.csv")             # just the CSVs in one job
    listJobFiles("my-batch-*", "*-scores.csv")  # one file across many jobs

BOTH arguments accept globs (`*`, `?`, `[...]`) and match the WHOLE name.
`fileName` defaults to "*", so a bare job name lists everything in it.

Pass the `s3Path` values you want to getJobFile(files=[...]) — one call for
the whole set. When your criterion cannot be written as a glob ("the newest
ten", "everything after run 28"), filter this result in code and pass the
paths you kept.

IMPORTANT: the returned s3Path also works directly in submitJob to chain
jobs — no need to download and re-upload.

Args:
    jobName: A job name, or a glob over job names (e.g. "my-batch-*"). Put
             as much LITERAL text as you can before the first wildcard —
             that prefix is what makes the search cheap. A pattern starting
             with a wildcard ("*-scores") has to walk every job you own and
             will usually time out.
    fileName: Glob over files within each job (default "*" = everything;
              e.g. "*-scores.csv"). Matches the whole name, and `*` spans

tools.name: mcp__Tamarind_Bio__saveAgent
tools.description:
Save one of the user's agents: a new one, a new version of one, or the Tamarind
agent; or publish or unpublish one. New chats get what is saved. Inside a Tamarind
chat the user is asked first: for the agent that chat runs as they choose where the
change lands (once, that chat, or all chats, that one included), and
a colleague's agent, which only its creator can save, still takes a proposal that
lands on that chat alone. A publish or an unpublish is asked about as itself.

To change one, read it with getAgentBuilder first and pass the version read. For a
saved agent send ONLY the keys that change: one left out keeps what is saved. For
`tamarind` send the whole definition back, with only what was asked changed.

Args:
    definition: {name, description, instructions,
        capabilities: {key: bool}, subagents: {name: bool},
        approvals: {action: "auto"|"ask"},
        job_types: [tool names] | null, blocked_job_types: [tool names],
        models: [modelId] | null,
        pipelines: [templateId] | null, skills: [built-in skill names] | null,
        allowed_sites: [exact hosts, no wildcards], allowed_packages: [package names],
        custom_skills: [{id, version?}], agent_subagents: [{id, version?}],
        model, effort, connectors: [{id?, name, url}]}.
        Only `name` is required for a new agent. null means every one; a capability
        or subagent left out stays on. Keys and names come from
        getAgentBuilder(what="catalog"), ids from what="skills" and what="agents".
        To block tools, set job_types null (every tool, ones added later too) and list
        the blocked ones in blocked_job_types; a job_types list replaces a block.
        Changing a saved agent: capabilities, subagents and approvals merge item by
        item (null resets one), and job_types, blocked_job_types, models, pipelines,
        skills, allowed_sites and allowed_packages also take
        {add: [...], remove: [...]}, except a list saved as null, which needs the
        whole list. Any other key replaces what is saved.

tools.name: mcp__Tamarind_Bio__searchMolecules
tools.description:
Query molecules across every group and run — filter and rank by TOOL SCORE, not
just by name.

This is the cross-run view. getPipelineRunResults(runId) answers "what did THIS
run produce, step by step"; this answers "across everything I have ever run,
which molecules score best" — and takes a run's `outputGroup` as `group` when
you want to narrow back down to one step.

Filtering is the point. `filter` takes repeatable `field:operator:value`
predicates, AND-ed, over metadata fields AND tool scores written as
`tool.metric`:
    filter=["alphafold.plddt:gt:0.8", "round:eq:2"]
Operators: gt, gte, lt, lte, eq, neq, and `field:exists` (metadata only).
`sortBy` takes the same `tool.metric` form, so you can rank by a score directly.

Each molecule is SUMMARIZED by default: id, name, type, `chains` (id, type,
length, sequence cut to 80 characters), `groups` (id, name), `metadata`
(your annotations only), `scores` (each tool's LATEST run; `scoreRuns` counts tools
run more than once) and `fileCounts` (files per producing tool). Pass full=true
for the API's complete molecule (every file with a download URL, every run's
scores); it is heavy, so keep `limit` small then and follow `nextCursor`.

Args:
    group: Only this group's molecules (a group id, or a step's `outputGroup`).
    jobName: Only molecules a job or batch produced or consumed, by name.
        Names are not unique; every visible match is included.
    jobId: The same, by id. Pass a batch id, not a child job id.
    type: Restrict to molecule kinds, e.g. ["protein"], ["small_molecule"].
    search: A term. With mode="default" (the default) it matches molecule
        NAMES. `matchedOn` says which field hit, and in practice it is always
        ["name"]: the documented metadata-key and score-metric matching does not
        fire, so searching for an annotation key returns an empty page with a NULL
        `nextCursor` — which per this tool's own contract means "finished, no
        matches", not "not implemented". To find molecules by an annotation, use
        `filter` instead (`filter=["my_key:exists"]`), which does match metadata.
        With mode="sequence" it is an amino-acid subsequence.
    mode: "default" or "sequence".
    filter: Repeatable `field:operator:value` predicates (max 32), AND-ed. `neq`
        also excludes molecules where the field is absent, so it is not the
        complement of `eq`.
    scope: "mine" (only groups YOU created) or "org" (your whole organization).
        Defaults to "mine" — EXCEPT when you pass `group`, where it defaults to
        "org", because a group id you were given is often a coworker's and "mine"
        would answer with an empty page. Pass "mine" explicitly to override that.
    sortBy: "id", "added", "type", "groupName", or a metadata field / tool
        score (`tool.metric`, on that tool's best run). A property no molecule
        here has is refused with code molecules_sort_property_not_found (the
        message names it); molecules missing a property others have sort last.
        A `tool.metric` score is not checked that way: sanity-check that the
        first item really does lead on that metric before acting on the order.
    dir: "asc" or "desc".
    limit: Molecules per page, 1-100 (default 25).
    cursor: `nextCursor` from the previous page.
    full: True returns each molecule exactly as the API does (files with signed
        download URLs and the full per-run score history) instead of the summary.

Returns:
    JSON: { items[], nextCursor, mode, scanProgress }. EITHER mode may return an
    EMPTY page while `nextCursor` is set — that means "keep paging", not "no
    results"; only a null `nextCursor` ends the search. In sequence mode
    `scanProgress` (0.0-1.0) tracks the scan.

tools.description:
Check, price or place ONE wet-lab assay order with a partner lab (Adaptyv, Ginkgo,
A-Alpha Bio). The same order fields in every mode:

  mode="validate" (default): check the order. Nothing is created, and the
      sequences are NOT sent to a lab. Answers `valid`; when false, `error` and
      `details` say what to fix. Run it until `valid` before the other modes.
  mode="estimate": price (USD) and turnaround. Creates nothing, but SENDS THE
      SEQUENCES TO THE LAB to be priced, so ask the user first.
      `estimatedCostUsd` is null for targets priced on request.
  mode="submit": place a real, paid order. Needs `idempotencyKey`. Tamarind
      reviews every order and arranges payment before the lab starts (a new
      order is `pending_approval`; nothing is charged here), but some labs
      receive the sequences at submit. Show the user the assay type, target,
      sequence count and any estimate, and get their OK first.

Workflow: listAssayTypes -> listAssayTargets (when the type has a
`targetsProvider`) -> this tool: validate, estimate (optional), submit ->
listAssays(assayId=...) to follow the order and fetch its results.

IDEMPOTENCY (submit). Use a new UUID per order. If a submit fails, times out or
its outcome is unclear, retry with the SAME key and SAME arguments: you get the
original order back (`idempotentReplay: true`), never a second one. Never reuse a
key for a different order (422).

Errors carry the platform's `code` and `error`, which say what to do; follow them
(they name REST routes: GET /assays is listAssays, the Idempotency-Key header is
`idempotencyKey`). In particular:
  - 409 `duplicate_order`: nothing was created; a recent order had the same assays
    and sequence count (`duplicateOfOrderId`). Ask the user whether they want a
    second, separately billed order. Only then resend with
    `confirmDuplicate=true` and a NEW idempotencyKey. Never set it on your own.
  - `teamNotified: true` (e.g. 409 `assays_blocked`, 502 `order_incomplete`): do
    not resubmit; Tamarind will follow up.
  - 403 `wetlab_access_required`: the account cannot order yet; the user can ask
    for access at `requestAccessUrl`.

Requests only ever go to the Tamarind platform (POST
https://app.tamarind.bio/api/validate-assay, /estimate-assay, /submit-assay).

Args:
    assayType: From listAssayTypes, e.g. "adaptyv_affinity".
    mode: "validate" (default), "estimate" or "submit".
    idempotencyKey: Required for mode="submit": a new UUID for this order (at
                    most 255 characters), reused only to retry it.
    sequences: Antibodies: "HEAVY:LIGHT" strings (or "HEAVY"), or
               {"name", "heavy", "light"} objects. Proteins: a string (chains
               joined with ":"), or {"name", "sequence"} objects. Names and
               sequences must all differ. Send this or csvFile.
    modality: "antibody" or "protein"; can be left out when the assay type
              takes only one.
    settings: The assay type's `settings`. A target goes in as `targetId`
              (Adaptyv), `targetIds` (A-Alpha Bio, a list) or `targetAntigen`
              (Ginkgo), using the `id` from listAssayTargets.
    csvFile: Instead of `sequences`: a CSV's path in your files (uploadFile it
             first). Needs columnMapping.
    columnMapping: The CSV's columns: `name`, `heavy`, `light` (antibodies) or
                   `name`, `sequence` (proteins).
    name: A name for the order (at most 200 characters).
    notes: For the Tamarind team reviewing it (at most 2000 characters).
    confirmDuplicate: Only after `duplicate_order`, and only when the user
                      wants the second order.

Returns:
    JSON with `mode`. validate: the verdict (`valid`, `error`, `details`, ...).
    estimate: the estimate. submit: success=true, `assay` (assayId, status,
    cancellable, resultsAvailable, ...) and `idempotentReplay`. A refusal in any
    mode: success=false, `backendStatus` and the platform's answer as sent.

```ts

// Columnmapping

// Confirmduplicate
```

tools.name: mcp__Tamarind_Bio__submitBatch
tools.description:
Submit MANY jobs as a SINGLE batch (one tool call, not one per job).

Submits the settings you construct to the Tamarind API
(POST https://app.tamarind.bio/api/submit-batch). Requests only ever go to
the Tamarind platform; the endpoint is fixed and not caller-controlled.

Protein Solubilization uses native Jobs: at most 500 exact input rows,
no batch parent or name prefixing. Read each results item's handoff and Id;
use getPipelineRun/getPipelineRunResults/stopPipelineRun for those IDs.
Supply submitId (a new UUID per intentional submission) and reuse the entire
unchanged request for retries. Batches require inputs: one list of prepared
pickerComplex references with complexId and groupId per settings row.
Call importMoleculeFile then getMoleculeImport until ingested before submission; omit pdbFile
when supplying prepared references.
The legacy parent/naming/budget rules below apply to other tools.

ALWAYS prefer this over calling submitJob in a loop. If you are about to
submit more than one job of the same `type`, use submitBatch instead — it
is one request, groups the jobs under a shared batch name, and is far
cheaper than N separate submissions.

But when `settings` holds exactly ONE entry, call submitJob instead. A
one-job batch is pure overhead: the platform writes a batch parent row
beside the single child and runs an aggregation pass to wrap it, and
nothing is being grouped.

Stay here even for a single job when the request needs something submitJob
cannot express — it takes only jobName, type and settings:
  - weightedHoursBudget, a runaway-cost cap. It is enforced off the batch
    parent row, so a single job without that row has no cap at all.
  - maxRuntimeSeconds, a per-job timeout.
  - fromFile (+ topN, sequenceField, sharedSettings). Reading the file,
    parsing it and ranking it all happen HERE, so such a request cannot be
    restated as a submitJob call — including when the file turns out to
    hold a single sequence.

Two ways to provide the per-job inputs:

1. settings + jobNames (explicit, full control):
   Provide an array of per-job settings objects and a matching array of
   job names. Use this when each job needs different parameters.

2. fromFile (a fasta or csv of sequences):
   Pass a workspace filename or a job s3Path (from listJobFiles) to a
   .fasta/.fa or .csv containing one sequence per record. Each sequence
   becomes one job. Prefer a curated file: the job's filtered_sequences.fa,
   or a fasta you uploaded with exactly the designs to run. A raw MPNN
   seqs/*.fa also carries the native input; its first, id-less native
   record is dropped automatically, but every other record is run.
   Example: submitBatch(batchName="fold-designs", type="alphafold",
                        fromFile="designs.fasta")

CHAINING FROM A FINISHED JOB (e.g. ProteinMPNN -> AlphaFold/Chai). There is
no mode that reads a job's output for you. Read the job's results yourself
(listJobFiles, then getJobFile on the sequence/metrics file), choose the
sequences to fold, and pass them as `settings` (one object per sequence) or
point `fromFile` at a curated fasta/csv — the job's filtered_sequences.fa,
or one you uploaded — rather than its raw seqs/*.fa. Nothing about the
downstream job's configuration comes from the source job, so set it here
(sharedSettings or per-row settings).

FINETUNE TOOLS. Training models in bulk works the same way: pass the
finetune tool (e.g. "chemprop-finetune") as `type`. Once the platform routes
finetune tools to its batch finetune endpoint (it refuses them here with code
"use_finetune_endpoint"), this tool resends the batch to POST /finetune-batch
once, automatically, with the tool under `model`; `endpoint` in the result says
which route accepted it. To train a single model, use submitFinetuningRun.

NAMING RULE. Never reuse `batchName` for one of the `jobNames`. The batch is itself a job
under that name, so a job sharing it collides and the batch never finishes; the server
rejects the submission with 400. The comparison is against the CLEANED name — characters
outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] are stripped and whitespace becomes "_", so a batch sent as
"my batch" is stored as "my_batch", and that is the value no job may equal.

Args:
    batchName: Unique name for the batch (also the prefix for auto job names).
    type: Tool to run for EVERY job in the batch (e.g. "alphafold", "chai").
          All jobs in a batch use the same tool. Use getJobSchema(type) for params.
    settings: (mode 1) Array of per-job settings objects.
    jobNames: (mode 1) Array of job names, same length as settings, and none equal
              to batchName (see NAMING RULE). For fromFile you can omit
              this — names are auto-generated as "{batchName}-1", "{batchName}-2", ...
    fromFile: (mode 2) Workspace path / job s3Path to a fasta or csv of sequences —
              preferably a curated one (filtered_sequences.fa or your upload).
    sequenceField: Settings field each sequence is placed into (default
                   "sequence" — correct for alphafold/chai/boltz/esmfold).
    topN: (fromFile) Keep only the top-N sequences (ranked by an
          MPNN/overall_confidence score in the file when available).
          Omit, or pass <=0, to fold ALL (default).
    sharedSettings: Settings applied to every job in any mode, e.g.
                    {"useMSA": true, "numModels": "5"}. In mode 1 a key
                    set in a job's own settings object wins over it.
                    validateJob takes no sharedSettings, so merge it
                    into every row and validate the whole list.
    maxRuntimeSeconds: Optional per-job timeout (integer seconds, >=1).
    weightedHoursBudget: Optional budget for the whole batch (number, >=0).
    projectTag: Organization project to file EVERY job in this batch under —
                its project id or its name. REQUIRED for orgs that have
                turned on "require a project tag"; those reject an untagged
                batch with 400 and a PERSONAL project does not count. The
                400 carries `availableProjects` (id + name), so retry with
                one of those rather than looking them up first. Ask the user
                which project when more than one could fit.

tools.name: mcp__Tamarind_Bio__submitFinetuningRun
tools.description:
Start ONE finetuning (model-training) run.

Finetuning trains a model on the user's own data (e.g. a property predictor
on a CSV of SMILES + measured values, or a protein language model on
labelled sequences). The run is an ordinary job — poll it with getJobs /
getJobLogs — and when it completes it registers a MODEL.

Submits to the Tamarind API (POST https://app.tamarind.bio/api/finetune).
Requests only ever go to the Tamarind platform; the endpoint is fixed and
not caller-controlled.

Workflow:
  1. Find finetuning tools: getAvailableModels() (train with the trainer,
     e.g. "chemprop-finetune", not the inference tool "chemprop-inference").
  2. Read its settings: getJobSchema(jobType="<model>"). Upload any
     training files first (uploadFile) and reference them by filename.
  3. Call this tool.
  4. The trained model appears in listFinetunedModels; it can run once its
     `status` is "Available".
  5. Run it with submitJob (or submitBatch): `type` = the model's
     `inferenceType`, `modelId` = the model's `id`.

Several training runs with one tool (a sweep): call submitBatch with the
finetune tool as `type` instead of calling this tool in a loop.

Args:
    model: The finetuning tool to train with — exact, case-sensitive name
           (e.g. "chemprop-finetune", "plm-finetune"). This is the field
           submitJob calls `type`. Use submitJob for ordinary tools: if
           `model` is not a finetuning tool (the platform answers
           "not_a_finetune_tool"), the connector resends it ONCE to
           POST /submit-job as an ordinary job; `endpoint` in the result
           names the route that accepted it.
    jobName: Name for the run (letters, digits, _ or -; max 100 chars).
             The trained model takes this name.
    settings: Training settings for `model` — see getJobSchema(jobType=model).
    parentModelId: Optional. Train the next VERSION of an existing model: its
                   `id` from listFinetunedModels (it must be trained with the
                   same tool). Sent as `settings.parentModelId`. Tools that do
                   not record lineage refuse it; `proteus` registers no model.
    projectTag: Organization project to file the run under — id or name.
                REQUIRED for orgs that turned on "require a project tag";
                the 400 then carries `availableProjects` to retry with.

Returns:
    JSON: success, jobName (the stored name to poll), model, and the
    backend response; on refusal an "error" plus any `code` /
    `availableProjects` / `hint` the platform sent.

```ts
// Jobname
jobName: string,
// Model
model: string,
// Parentmodelid
parentModelId?: string, // default: null
// Projecttag
projectTag?: string, // default: null
// Settings
settings: { [key: string]: any },
}): Promise<// _WrappedResult
{
// Result
result: string,
}>;
```
